Named entity recognition (NER) stands as a pivotal task in natural language processing and information extraction, aiming to identify semantically significant terms within text, such as persons, organizations, and locations. To address this, we introduced NESTAD, an innovative transformation that converts the task to operate on a linear sequence of entities rather than raw character data. The core mechanism of NESTAD is a hierarchical sorting strategy that reorders overlapping based on their types, effectively creating a non-redundant representation suitable for standard sequence models. To validate our hypothesis that such a reduction to non-overlapping structures is viable, we devised an learning methodology capable of learning these distinct entity characteristics independently. We evaluated our M2 model's efficacy through extensive tests on two benchmark datasets, comparing it against current state-of-the-art sequence-dependent models that process characters directly; the results demonstrate superior performance by the proposed approach when evaluating both overall efficiency. Beyond empirical performance, this work also advances the theoretical framework of natural language structure modeling and offers foundational insights for future advancements in the entity extraction landscape.

The inability of the Standard Model to explain neutrino mass constitutes one of the most significant challenges in particle physics. Consequently, this alternative pathway implies that next-generation $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay experiments will not be able to detect neutrino mass if the mechanism involves ultra-light dark matter interaction. Furthermore, if this scenario is the true origin of neutrino mass, it generates new signatures in cosmological datasets—including those from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and large-scale structure surveys—as well as alterations to neutrino physics involving cosmic rays and various astrophysical systems such as supernovae and the equation of state of neutron stars.

Consequently, such limitations may impair the quality of decisions made within both personal and professional contexts.

To the extent of our knowledge, we offer the first end-to-end interpretability framework for GNNs trained on learned, sparsified graphs. CountSketch is an established dimensionality reduction method that projects vectors into lower-dimensional spaces via a carefully constructed adaptive sketched vector, a capability that has led to widespread adoption in various streaming algorithms. We introduce a novel technique, the Random Partition Argument (APA), which unifies and improves existing results while extending their applicability. Utilizing this framework, we demonstrate that an adversary capable of dynamically choosing entries for all incoming vectors can only increase the error by a polylogmic factor, a strong guarantee especially considering the algorithm's computational simplicity. Furthermore, we show that an adversary permitted to modify small constants in the matrix generation process can likewise elevate the adversary-controlled error term by at most such a polylogmic factor. In terms of practical application, we enhance several previous theoretical findings and refine the randomized error bounds, providing a more probabilistic analysis of the adaptive adversary term.

This study examines how charge-carrier outflows from nanoscale gaps affect gap-plasmons, an phenomenon attributable to two main factors: optical nonlocality and electron outflows. We establish that $t_{_{0}}$—representing the characteristic length of the system—is equivalent to $v_{F}\sqrt{\Gamma/t_{0}}$—representing the system's length. Given that the optical response differs based on which scale dominates, an investigation of the geometric arrangement of the conductive layers allows estimation of parameters $\Gamma$ and $t_{_{0}}$. Numerical tests on a gold dimer confirm the model, revealing nonlocal and electron outflow regimes for specific inter-laminar distances and parameter sets. Notably, for gaps of approximately 0.5 nm with a $\Gamma$ of 2.55 eV or 0.1 nm with a $\Gamma$ of 0.95 eV, one may anticipate the dominant electron outflow.

Object-oriented programming languages offer significant advantages in terms of development efficiency, maintainability, extensibility, and code reuse, yet writing parallel programs for GPUs remains challenging because of architecture-mismatching models and memory allocation driver limitations. This paper introduces DYNASOAR, a dynamic native static object-aware memory allocator designed specifically for GPUs. SOAR aligns with common object-oriented conventions by utilizing dynamic, type-specific heap allocators inherent to programming languages, while dynamically resolving per-thread local static stacks of varying sizes at compile time to ensure optimal thread-safe memory access patterns. Further enhancing efficiency, SOAR resolves dynamic linking conflicts between the allocator and unified memory access commands by dynamically reordering bytes per thread during memory access without altering the dynamic bit-level structure. Our experimental results demonstrate that DynaSOAR significantly improves runtime execution time and memory bandwidth compared to existing solutions, with development efficiency remaining equivalent.

A signed graph consists of a vertex set partitioned into two groups, traditionally indicated by edges that are either unweighted or carry positive weight, versus edges that are weighted negatively. A well-known result by Zaslavski, extending a theorem by Rosenfeld concerning the expansion of simple graphs, demonstrates that nearly all signed graphs possess a sufficiently large doubled version. The current paper presents the opposite finding: it proves that nearly all infinite limits of symmetric 1-wrapped manifolds admit a non-manifold structure. The proof of this result draws on characteristics of the homogeneous limit of such structures demonstrated to possess certain distinctive combinatorial features.

This study examines how the conditions of canonical equilibrium translate within the Weyl-Wigner framework. We derive the corresponding Weyl matrix forms and associated Wigner functions for both temperature and pressure balance. Furthermore, this paper investigates the statistical behaviors of Weyl operators and Wigner functions for a system in causal and thermal equilibrium. Finally, we formulate the characteristic function for a Weyl-Wigner ensemble that is both causal and thermally canonical.

This paper establishes both direct and inverse results concerning the size of bounded signed sum sets for integers within the range $[1,n]$ that meet specific constraints. In particular, we generalize an earlier finding by Robbach regarding constrained sum sets and introduce new extensions of Freiman's $3c$ theorem, covering the case of bounded integers in $[1,n]$ subject to such restrictions.

Characterizing cancer and related disorders often relies on analyzing biopsied and subsequently stained tissue samples (histopathology), a process that necessitates skilled professional interpretation to yield a diagnostic conclusion. While this analysis is executed by seasoned experts, their work frequently incorporates subjective elements, influencing both the methodology adopted and the final outcomes. A primary hurdle in automating histopathological assessment is the scarcity of publicly available, comprehensively labeled digital datasets suitable for training machine learning models. To overcome this limitation, we present UniToPatho, a unified dataset comprising 2,342 images of colored rectal polyps, supplemented by detailed annotations regarding morphological features, architectural patterns, and the degree of adenomatous transformation. This collection enables a wide range of tools for analyzing intracellular polyp imagery and performing related tasks. Our experimental evaluations utilize k-means clustering, random forest algorithms, and ConvNeXt-Vit to validate these capabilities. It is important to acknowledge that further expansions of the dataset would benefit from the collaborative synthesis of contributions from multiple researchers.

We propose an adjustable finite element method for anistic diffusion problems on bounded domains, characterized Coefficients that vary gradually. Our approach involves augmenting the standard equation with auxiliary variables and applying variable transformation techniques, allowing us to elevate the equation's order while keeping oscillatory coefficients smooth. This strategy yields a five-point high-order formulation on a single standard mesh, resulting in an efficient numerical scheme with just 25 degrees of freedom per mesh. Mathematical analysis supports this approach, demonstrating that only minimal regularity conditions are required in the domain and for the coefficients, and confirming fourth-order accuracy in both $C0$-continuous $H^1$ norms and $L^1$ contexts. Furthermore, extensive numerical experiments validate the methodology, verifying its high accuracy and versatility.

The Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites exhibit a composition resembling H chondrites but are deficient in water and radiogenic noble gases typically found in ordinary chondrites. This anomaly suggests these planetesimals did not remain in a wet, water-rich environment like those that produced standard H chondrites. Instead, we propose that the thermal events responsible for the loss of volatile compounds in Chelyabinsk and Benenitra occurred because planetesimals migrated to higher orbital temperatures in the inner solar system while still in a wet state. This migration triggered the entrapment of water vapor within crystalline voids of phosphates and subsequent thermal cracking or impact-related impacts that caused the loss of these gases. Consequently, these events explain observed patterns regarding asteroids' craters and radiogenic noble gas concentrations within inner solar system planetesimals.

Recently applicable in the study of higher-spin XXZ models outside their thermodynamic limit, a newly proposed technique is detailed that relies on the novel construction of higher-order cycle matrices via the repeated application of the Bethe-anomaly. These higher-order cycle matrices exhibit significant interest because they factorize completely when computing the dynamical structure factors associated with integer-momentum injections into the higher-spin XXZ systems thermodynamically in the ground state. Additionally, these higher-order cycle matrices display intriguing higher-spin analogues of both affine quantum-group multiplication and Yangian compositeness properties. Ultimately, these higher-order cycle matrices fully embody the integrability and higher-spin analogues of affine quantum-group symmetry of the model.

Standard multipolar expansions, which rely on the long wavelength limit, typically retain only a constrained set (e.g., a dipole and quadrupole moment pair) of terms. However, our investigation demonstrates that accurately modeling scattering and additive contributions to multipole dipoole moments requires considering the full infinite series. We derive closed-form expressions for the entire series regarding a sphere and additional geometric configurations. While a general tensor formulation for individual moments is provided, we specifically calculate the optical force and velocity vectors associated with an infinite sequence of these dipoole moments for a sphere and spherically symmetric structures. Our results indicate the necessity of an "electric multipole dipoole moment" definition, requiring both magnitude and orientation, to fully capture electric multipole dipoole moment effects. Finally, our method is validated by comparing traditional approximations with new results, showing excellent agreement within regimes where the electric field dipoole moment is small.

This study offers explicit characterizations of the symmetric-group-algebra elements known as double Young-Capelli bitableaux, which are crucial for investigating the shift of the Young symmetric functions character of the infinite symmetric group. These bitableaux form a dual basis to the collection of immanant-bitableaux within the algebra, a relationship that enables the development of specific presentations for the relative Schur algebra, denoted as $S\mathbb{Q}(\infty|n)$. Furthermore, we provide defining presentations for the subalgebra of the symmetric algebra generated by double Young bitableaux of rectangular shape and introduce the quantum immanant as a natural deformation of the classical immanant function.

Deforming the features of chest X-rays (CXR) associated with disease could aid in enhancing the accuracy of automated diagnosis models for pneumonia and other thoracic disorders. Although existing methods allow researchers to manipulate these radiographs to reflect changes in clinical categories or textures, they lack specificity regarding actual pathology, often resulting in adverse side effects like artifacts or distorted anatomical structures. Additionally, the potential impacts of such modifications on future medical diagnosis remain insufficiently evaluated. This paper introduces an evaluation framework designed to comprehensively assess the effects of altering CXR sickness-related features. Building on this foundation, we propose a new methodology for transforming CXR pathology-specific markers. Our approach utilizes a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) trained on paired instances of healthy and pneumonia-infested imagery to isolate and alter such attributes. Tests indicate our framework effectively measures modification consequences, notably validating improvements in performance across multiple pneumonia detection models.

ViDaExpert serves as a specialized instrument designed to facilitate the representation and analysis of user-input vector datasets. Recognizing that data analysis is integral to decision-making within business and business-adjacent contexts, ViDaExpert prioritizes accessibility, aiming to enable professionals to conduct sophisticated visual analyses without reliance on programming languages or language-specific libraries. The application employs PyDA—a custom visual analysis model to depict high-dimensional, sparse vector data. The core functionality of ViDAExpert revolves around presenting complex, multi-faceted data in user-friendly dashboards. By facilitating these operations, the tool helps analysts derive insights and support decision-making within professional and quasi-professional domains.

Calculating the potential of mass or charge distributions via Newtonian formulas is essential in both geophysics and other scientific domains. Nevertheless, evaluating these calculations can present major hurdles when dealing with complex shapes or nonuniform densities. This study proposes utilizing triangulated nets for such configurations and calculating the potential associated with each net individually. This method requires determining the potential generated by a uniform sphere sector defined by two planar cones sharing a common axis but differing in angle and a second term that accounts for the distance between the sphere sector's central axis and the source's uniform momentum center. This cumbersome exact formula was found to be highly repetitive and was therefore simplified into a much more manageable closed form. Together, these formulas enable efficient and precise computation of the Newtonian potential and related quantities, such as gravitational acceleration, for regulated triangulated nets.
